reasoning_traces.think:
The MAML adapter operates under a first-order optimization scheme where only intercept shifts are updated during regime transitions, avoiding overfitting on small support sets. This aligns with the principle of minimal intervention in Bayesian updating. The NGGP leverages Laplace approximations to provide calibrated uncertainty estimates, enabling robust inference even under limited data. Drift detection uses a majority-vote ensemble of multiple detectors (ADWIN, HDDM-A, etc.) to identify both abrupt and gradual shifts in performance metrics. These primitives form a coherent system for adaptive learning and inference in evolving environments.
